item.title: Drone strike kills 28 at crowded market in Sudan
item.description:
A drone strike hit a bustling market in the town of Ghabesh in Sudan's West Kordofan state on Tuesday, killing at least 28 people and wounding dozens more, according to local rights monitors.

The attack, reported by the Emergency Lawyers group, marks the latest in a relentless wave of drone warfare against civilian targets in Sudan's Kordofan region, where fighting between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces has intensified in recent months.

item.title: EU reaches deal to cut US import duties ahead of Trump's tariff deadline
item.description:
European Union negotiators reached a provisional agreement early Wednesday on legislation to eliminate import duties on US goods, clearing a critical hurdle in the bloc's race to comply with President Donald Trump's July 4 ultimatum before tariffs on European exports escalate sharply.

The deal, struck after a final round of trilogue talks between the European Parliament and the Council of the EU in Strasbourg, finalizes the legislative framework needed to implement the Turnberry Agreement — the trade pact reached between Trump and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen at Trump's Scottish golf resort in July 2025.

item.title: NATO weighs Hormuz mission as top commander confirms talks
item.description: NATO is actively discussing the possibility of deploying a military mission to the Strait of Hormuz if the critical waterway remains blocked beyond early July, according to Bloomberg reporting confirmed by alliance officials. The deliberations mark a potential turning point for the alliance, which has so far avoided direct involvement in the broader U.S.-Iran conflict.

item.title: Chile's Kast fires security minister in first cabinet shake-up
item.description: Chilean President José Antonio Kast carried out his first cabinet reshuffle on Tuesday, removing Security Minister Trinidad Steinert and Government Spokesperson Mara Sedini just over two months into his administration, in a shake-up that underscores growing unease over his government's handling of its core policy promise: fighting crime.

item.title: Putin hails 'unprecedented' Russia-China ties in Beijing talks with Xi
item.description: Russian President Vladimir Putin met with Chinese President Xi Jinping at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing on Wednesday, hailing relations between the two countries as having reached an "unprecedentedly high level" and calling for a more balanced international order as trade and energy ties continue to expand.

item.title: US and Israel planned to install Ahmadinejad after Iran war began
item.description:
The United States and Israel entered the February 2026 war against Iran with a secret plan to elevate former president Mahmoud Ahmadinejad as the country's new leader following the assassination of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, according to a New York Times report published on May 19 citing US officials.

The revelation exposes the full scope of the regime-change ambitions underlying Operation Epic Fury, the US military campaign, and Israel's Operation Roaring Lion, which began with massive airstrikes on February 28, 2026.

item.title: Xi and Putin condemn Golden Dome at Beijing summit
item.description: Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin used a high-profile summit in Beijing on Wednesday to jointly condemn the United States' Golden Dome missile defense program, calling it "an obvious threat to strategic stability" and warning that it risked turning outer space into a theater of war.

item.title: Samsung union suspends strike after last-minute deal
item.description: Samsung Electronics and its largest labor union reached a tentative agreement on Wednesday evening, suspending a general strike by nearly 48,000 workers that had been set to begin Thursday. The deal came after Labor Minister Kim Young-hoon personally intervened to broker a last-ditch negotiation session, stepping in hours after talks at the National Labor Relations Commission collapsed earlier in the day.

item.title: Barney Frank, gay rights pioneer in Congress, dies at 86
item.description:
Former Massachusetts Congressman Barney Frank, one of the first openly gay members of Congress and co-author of the landmark Dodd-Frank Wall Street Reform Act, has died at age 86. His sister, Ann Lewis, confirmed the news to NBC News on Wednesday.

Frank died at his home in Ogunquit, Maine, where he had been in hospice care since late April due to congestive heart failure. He is survived by his husband, Jim Ready, whom he married in 2012.

item.title: OpenAI prepares to submit confidential IPO filing within days
item.description:
OpenAI is working with Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley on a confidential IPO prospectus that could be filed with the Securities and Exchange Commission within days, according to reports, as the ChatGPT maker accelerates its path toward what would be one of the largest public offerings in history.

The filing would come just days after a California jury unanimously dismissed Elon Musk's lawsuit against OpenAI, removing what many viewed as the most pressing legal obstacle to the company's public listing.

item.title: EU calls treatment of Gaza flotilla activists 'completely unacceptable'
item.description: The European Commission on Wednesday declared that the treatment of detained Gaza flotilla activists shown in a video released by Israeli National Security Minister Itamar Ben Gvir was "completely unacceptable," joining a growing chorus of international condemnation that has triggered a diplomatic crisis for Israel.

item.title: UN General Assembly votes 141-8 to back climate ruling over US objections
item.description:
The United Nations General Assembly on Wednesday voted overwhelmingly to adopt a resolution endorsing the International Court of Justice's landmark advisory opinion that countries have a legal obligation to protect the planet from climate change. The vote was 141 in favor, 8 against, and 28 abstentions.

The resolution, spearheaded by the small Pacific island nation of Vanuatu, calls on states to comply with their obligations under international law, including adopting national climate action plans to limit global temperature rise to 1.5°C above pre-industrial levels and transitioning away from fossil fuels. The countries that voted against were Belarus, Iran, Israel, Liberia, Russia, Saudi Arabia, the United States, and one other nation.

item.title: Trump and Netanyahu clash in tense call over Iran peace framework
item.description: President Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held what sources described as a "lengthy and dramatic" phone call Tuesday evening over a proposed framework to end the war with Iran, exposing a widening rift between the two allies over how to conclude the months-long conflict.

item.title: IRGC warns war will spread beyond Middle East if US resumes strikes
item.description:
Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps issued a stark warning on Wednesday that any renewed American or Israeli military action against the country would trigger a conflict extending far beyond the Middle East, promising "crushing blows in places you cannot even imagine."

The threat came as diplomatic signals suggested a potential path toward ending the nearly three-month-old war between the US-Israel coalition and Iran. President Donald Trump told lawmakers that the conflict could end "very quickly," while Vice President JD Vance said negotiations with Tehran are "in a pretty good spot," adding that "a lot of good progress is being made."

item.title: Beijing delays Pentagon official's visit over Taiwan arms deal
item.description:
Beijing is stalling a planned visit by Elbridge Colby, the Pentagon's under-secretary of defense for policy, as China pressures President Donald Trump over a $14 billion weapons package for Taiwan, according to a Financial Times report published Wednesday.

The delay comes just days after Trump's two-day summit with Chinese President Xi Jinping in Beijing on May 14-15, during which Taiwan emerged as one of the most contentious issues. Reuters was unable to independently confirm the details of the FT report.

item.title: Ukrainian drone strikes bring central Russia's oil refining to a standstill
item.description: A sustained campaign of Ukrainian drone strikes has forced virtually all major oil refineries in central Russia to halt or scale back fuel production, bringing refining operations across the region to a near-standstill, Reuters reported on May 20. The disruptions mark one of the most concentrated blows to Russian energy infrastructure since the start of the full-scale war.

item.title: Merz proposes EU 'associate membership' for Ukraine
item.description:
German Chancellor Friedrich Merz has formally proposed granting Ukraine "associate member" status in the European Union, outlining the plan in a letter to EU chiefs Ursula von der Leyen and António Costa made public on Thursday.

The proposal would allow Ukraine's leader to attend EU summits and ministerial meetings without voting rights, while Kyiv would also gain a non-voting representative on the European Commission and non-voting members of the European Parliament.

item.title: Turkey sends flights to repatriate Gaza flotilla activists detained by Israel
item.description:
Israel has begun deporting approximately 430 activists detained from the Global Sumud Flotilla after Israeli naval forces intercepted the Gaza-bound aid convoy in international waters west of Cyprus, a move that has triggered a wave of international condemnation intensified by a video posted by far-right National Security Minister Itamar Ben-Gvir showing him taunting bound detainees.

The deportations, confirmed on Wednesday, follow days of mounting diplomatic fallout after Ben-Gvir shared footage of himself confronting kneeling activists with their hands zip-tied behind their backs, waving an Israeli flag and reportedly shouting "We are the masters" as Israel's national anthem played in the background. Turkey said on Thursday it was sending charter flights to Israel to repatriate its nationals among the detained activists.

item.title: Iran's Supreme Leader orders enriched uranium to stay in country
item.description: A directive from Iran's Supreme Leader that the country's near-weapons-grade enriched uranium must remain on Iranian soil jolted markets on Thursday, erasing much of the optimism that had briefly lifted investor sentiment a day earlier.

item.title: Iran restarted drone production during ceasefire, US intelligence finds
item.description:
Iran has restarted drone production during the six-week ceasefire that began in early April, rebuilding its military industrial base at a pace that has caught US intelligence agencies off guard, CNN reported Thursday citing four sources familiar with the assessments.

The reporting contradicts weeks of public assurances from Trump administration officials and military leaders who characterized Iran's military as crippled beyond near-term repair following Operation Epic Fury, the US-Israeli bombing campaign that began in late February.
